spec_notes: The spec (ratchet/spec.md) leaves most of my items Open for the requester (C-14 token precedence and refused env token, C-19 naming, C-21 labels, C-23 restoration, C-31 sends while pending, C-34 auto retry, C-35/C-39 library scope and name conflicts, C-37/C-38 instruction edit/delete, C-47 forget matching, C-50 id/type/readers, C-51 preview id, C-55/C-60 pending proposals, C-62 stale confirm, C-68 away period, C-69 several tasks, C-71 in-flight step, C-75 restart, C-79 widths), yet the product decides each one without saying in the spec that it did; several of these decisions are told in the README (env precedence, copy on Use, ids at confirmation, expiry of stale previews, in-flight discard). Discovery clauses C-83 to C-98 pin behaviours of this build that a correct product need not share (a browser submission journal and receipt check, exact-amount rules up to 9007199254740991, complete-ID rule for lookups, length-limit handling). The spec contradicts the product in two places: C-97 says over-limit editor text must not be silently clipped, but the Task request, Instruction text, Memory text and Bot name inputs clip silently via maxlength; C-98 says an overlapping second instance on one DATA_DIR must be refused or keep both writes, but it is accepted and one order is lost. Silent where the product decides: one shared working copy of records (U-36), all-tasks Tasks region (U-37), parallel tasks (U-38), no completion message (U-40), focus placement (U-58), unexpected-error logging (U-60).
tests_notes: Five broad scenario tests carry most coverage and each checks many behaviours at once (for example "setup, record scoping, saved workspace and transparent provider echo" covers setup, token file mode, redaction, bots, memory edit/forget, rename, record counts for three people, restore of place and refused proposals; "reply reservations, library state and original history survive navigation" covers dedup, pending sends, person switching, retry, instructions and saved tasks). Several tests are tied to internals: build-3 storage test mocks fs.renameSync and fs.fsyncSync; the CLI test asserts the folder holds exactly ["state.json"] and a symlink; tests build Chat and Store objects directly and call chat.receipt. Several would fail on another correct build: exact notice texts (/No step was added/, /editable field/, /whole amount/, /range or precision/, /check the full record ID/), the label format ending "Chat 2" and "Bot #3", provider-token file mode 0600, proposal result.status "expired", the turn.notice field, created ids exactly ORD-1005/ORD-1006 in a set, and the copy-on-Use semantic for deleted instructions. No test covers the page itself (Since you were away, narrow layout, focus, live polling, Memory text prefill), duplicate-name refusal for saved entries, or rename through Edit.
maintainer: The submission/receipt protocol spans app.js (sessionStorage journal, epochs, receipt polling) and chat.js (submission ids, generations, attempt numbers); changing either side without the other risks duplicated or lost turns, and only part of it is tested. Every mutation goes through Store.transact with a full structuredClone and whole-file rewrite plus the strict readState validator, so adding any field to the saved state requires updating the validator or the app refuses to start on its own data. Record request parsing in lib/records.js re-implements and rewrites the stand-in's command grammar (field-name lowercasing, marker-preserving rewrite, id checks), which must be kept in step with provider/standin.js.
